decisions.selected: Measure cache-strategy findings resolved by merged workflow changes rather than workflow activity.
decisions.rationale: The adoption-time mission is to identify repeated cache problems and raise actionable issues; creation and issue closure alone do not demonstrate the cache strategy changed.

decisions.selected: Assign the linked [cache-strategy] issues whose bodies name the workflow run URL.
alternatives: Assign every cache-memory workflow examined that day
decisions.rationale: The issue template embeds the producing run URL, which provides a stable, reconstructable ownership key without relying on agent logs.

decisions.selected: Accept a completed linked issue only when a timeline-linked PR merged a workflow-file change.
alternatives: Completed issue without a merged workflow change
decisions.rationale: The issue and merged workflow change are durable repository evidence of an assigned remediation; logs and output creation are activity evidence.

decisions.selected: Use linked issues resolved with qualifying merged workflow changes divided by linked issues.
decisions.rationale: The proportion measures full attainment for all findings assigned to one run without combining operational attainment with diagnostics.
The adoption-time workflow uses a seven-day issue-output expiry and a seven-day cache-hit threshold, providing a frozen, workflow-specific horizon.
The [cache-strategy] assignment prefix was introduced in the adoption commit, so no pre-adoption cases are comparable under this contract.

uncertainties.description: GitHub issue search or issue-state evidence can be unavailable during replay.
uncertainties.mitigation: Return null rather than treating unavailable evidence as a missed remediation.

uncertainties.description: A completed issue does not establish that this workflow caused the remediation.
